title: Hijaiyah Letter Pronunciation Audio Dataset for Articulation Characteristic Classification
abstract: This dataset contains audio recordings of Arabic (hijaiyah) letters pronounced correctly and incorrectly, collected to support research on automatic classification of letter pronunciation characteristics (sifat huruf) in Quranic recitation learning. Content - 21,600 WAV recordings, balanced between two classes: "Data Benar" (correct pronunciation, 10,800 files) and "Data Salah" (incorrect pronunciation, 10,800 files). - Each class has 20 numbered sub-folders; each sub-folder holds the recordings of one respondent (540 files per sub-folder). - Each respondent pronounced 36 items (the 28 hijaiyah letters plus letter variants), each with 3 vowel marks (harakat: 1 = fathah, 2 = kasrah, 3 = dhammah), repeated 5 times. - Recordings are mono, mostly 44.1 kHz (a few at 48 kHz), and about 0.7-1.0 seconds long. - File naming: --.wav, e.g. 21-1-1.wav = item 21, fathah, repetition 1. Annotation Each letter is annotated with 12 binary/ternary label variables covering 18 articulation characteristics (sifat huruf), following Al-Hafiz (2014). Five variables encode opposing pairs (S) and seven encode characteristics without an opposite (T): S1: jahr = 0 / hams = 1 S2: rakhawah = 0 / bayniyyah = 1 / syiddah = 2 S3: istifal = 0 / isti'la = 1 S4: infitah = 0 / ithbaq = 1 S5: ishmat = 0 / idzlaq = 1 T1 shafir, T2 qalqalah, T3 liin, T4 inhirah, T5 takrir, T6 tafasysyi, T7 istithaalah (1 = present, 0 = absent). Labels follow the letter and, for some letters, the vowel mark (e.g. tafkhim of some letters depends on the vowel). In the accompanying article, three properties are modelled: S1 (jahr-hams), S3 (tarqiq-tafkhim) and T2 (qalqalah). For the incorrect class, the label of these three properties is the inverse of the correct label of the same item. [Fill in: label convention for the incorrect class for the other nine properties, or state that they are given for the correct class only.] The documentation lists the exact rules, the 9 recordings with non-standard file names excluded from experiments (21,591 recordings used), and respondent sub-folders that contain identical recordings. Additional files - Label and index tables (one row per recording, with respondent and cross-validation group). - Respondent-level train/test split (seed 42) and 5-fold cross-validation assignment. - Source code for preprocessing (resampling, voice activity detection, noise reduction, trimming, normalisation), augmentation (time stretching, pitch shifting, additive noise, time shifting), feature extraction (MFCC, Mel spectrogram, LPC) and model training. Intended use Training and evaluating classifiers for letter pronunciation characteristics. Because several recordings per respondent exist, splits must be made at respondent level to avoid data leakage; augmented copies must follow the split of their source recording.

title: STUDENT LEARNING USING AI
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a way to make digital learning more responsive to students’ individualneeds. This paper proposes an AI-assisted student learning system that combines learner preferences, topic-level progress, practiceresponses, and teacher feedback to recommend suitable learning resources and next-step activities. The proposed framework includesa learner interface, a content repository, a recommendation and feedback engine, progress analytics, and teacher oversight. Ratherthan treating a single score as a complete picture of ability, the system uses repeated learning evidence to identify topics that mayneed revision and to suggest practice at an appropriate level. The design emphasizes explainable recommendations, privacy,accessibility, and human supervision. A prototype could be developed using a web interface, a structured content store, and rulebased or machine-learning components selected according to available data. Evaluation should measure recommendation relevance,consistency, usability, learner engagement, and learning outcomes through a controlled and ethically approved study. Noexperimental performance is claimed in this conceptual paper; the framework and evaluation plan are presented for futureimplementation.

title: No Species Is an Island, Entire of Itself: Genetic Speciation Algorithm with Interplay among Species
abstract: This paper, with a particular emphasis on Genetic Algorithm (GA), proposes a novel approach that integrates clustering mechanisms, predator-prey dynamics, and a distinctive selection strategy for generating subsequent populations. The proposed evolutionary algorithm, referred to as Genetic Speciation Algorithm with Interplay Among Species (GSAIS), is comprehensively evaluated against several variants of GAs as well as a set of widely adopted state-of-the-art optimization algorithms, recognized among the top-performing winners of recent Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) competitions. This thorough comparative study is performed using the most well-established benchmark functions, covering unimodal, multimodal, hybrid, and composition optimization landscapes. The experiments are conducted on medium-, and large-scale problem instances to evaluate the robustness, scalability, convergence behavior, and solution quality of GSAIS across diverse optimization scenarios. The GSAIS achieved rank 2nd, and 1st against the competitors in medium- and large- scale benchmark problems, respectively based on the Friedman Test with receiving 40.3% of top ranking along all instances based on best found and standard deviation rankings. Extensive statistical and computational results demonstrate the effectiveness of GSAIS, highlighting its superior performance in achieving global optimization. The ablation study and sensitivity analysis reveals the positive effect of the incorporated mechanisms in GSAIS in finding global optimization, especially in large scale problems. The findings establish GSAIS as a potential candidate method for addressing optimization problems and underscore its potential to advance the design of next-generation evolutionary algorithms.

title: Grown reasoning transfers: a sealed test of reasoning grown from operations of mind
abstract: LOCUS is a research programme building a mind that runs on ordinary CPUs, with no neural network and no pretraining. This technical note reports where it stands on 25 October 2026. It sets out the full framework, resting on the Expectational Meaning Hypothesis (knowing what something means is knowing what to expect from it) and Operations of Mind (reasoning can grow by itself from a few basic mental operations), and reports the sealed Phase 2 test, T20. Reasoning chains grown in one world, frozen and tested from an empty memory, beat no growth in a world never seen in training or development (+0.0135 in prediction score, 6 of 12 lifetimes, both lower bounds above zero), and growth repeatedly found the same strategy: borrow a memory, judge the borrow, use it only if it holds. The headline claim, that grown chains beat no growth in their own worlds, is not licensed, because its control was confirmed once in 16 re-checks against a bar of zero set in advance. A systematic search of seven fields found no prior system that keeps a change to its own reasoning only when the change beats the same change run with its memory scrambled. The note closes with the next frame: operations that respond to the situation, effort that scales with misfit, and the sceptic as the only selector. Every sealed result was pre-registered, independently audited, frozen by hash, run once and independently re-derived. The engine is not released.

title: Code and aggregate inputs for Prioritising anaemia follow-up after infection-related hospitalisation: a retrospective comparison of clinical information and prediction targets
abstract: Code and aggregate inputs for an exploratory MIMIC-IV v3.1 study comparing clinical information, prediction targets and selection-list size for identifying 30-day same-hospital returns accompanied by initial haemoglobin below 8 g/dL among adults discharged with haemoglobin 8–<10 g/dL after infection-related care. The release provides aggregate arithmetic checks, eight-figure replay, selected laboratory/cohort/model functions, synthetic tests, tested dependencies, a concise run README, licences and checksums. It is not a complete validated raw-data-to-manuscript pipeline. Confidence intervals are read from saved aggregates and are not recomputed from patient-level predictions. No restricted records, identifiers, individual predictions, clinical notes or individual case-review answers are included. Source-data analysis requires independent credentialed access to MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-Note through PhysioNet. Copyright (c) 2026 Zhiqiang Hu and Jihui Ye. Author-original code and tests are MIT licensed; original aggregate inputs, documentation and reproduced figures are CC BY 4.0. Dependencies and restricted source data retain their applicable terms. See README.md and LICENSES/ for the licence scope and complete texts.

title: The Post-Byte Era: TIT BIT and TIT GIT as Z₅-Graded Structural Primitives for Quantum-Resilient Computation
abstract: The Post-Byte Era: TIT BIT and TIT GIT as Z₅-Graded Structural Primitives for Quantum-Resilient Computation C. J Tully Founder, Ly-Algebra Framework & 5-Fold Symmetry Platform Independent Researcher, Engineer, Tamworth, NSW, Australia ORCID: 0009-0007-5661-7332 25th October 2026 Abstract This paper introduces the TIT BIT and TIT GIT as foundational primitives for a post-binary computing paradigm. The TIT BIT is realized as a node in a five-dimensional \mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}-graded vector space equipped with a bilinear product whose structure constants encode golden-ratio scaling. The Quasi-Equivalence Index (QEI) is derived directly from the graded square of this product and supplies a deterministic integrity gate. TIT GIT is defined as a version-control system that tracks structural coherence rather than raw bytes and signs commits with hybrid post-quantum signatures. The construction unifies geometry, non-associative algebra, and cryptography into a single data unit. Keywords: Ly-Algebra; TIT BIT; TIT GIT; Quasi-Equivalence Index; \mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}-grading; golden ratio; post-quantum cryptography.

title: Pre-specified benchmark of a slice-based transfer pipeline for lung-nodule malignancy with external validation on LUNA25
abstract: This dataset contains the complete outputs of a pre-specified benchmark of a slice-based ImageNet-transfer pipeline for lung-nodule malignancy classification on NoduleMNIST3D (64 x 64 x 64 CT crops, MedMNIST v2) and of its external validation on the LUNA25 public development set (6,163 nodules from 2,120 screening participants). Thirty-one arms were trained: 24 ConvNeXt-Tiny configurations crossing slice view, pooling over slices, augmentation granularity and fine-tuning depth (5 seeds each), five standard baselines (frozen ConvNeXt-Tiny linear probe, fine-tuned ResNet-18, ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B0 and DenseNet-121) and two 3D networks (3D ResNet-18 and ACS ResNet-18), each with 15 seeds, plus the selected configuration retrained to 15 seeds, 235 models in all. The design, the selection record, an external-validation addendum and one deviation (field of view of the external images) were hashed before the data they govern were read. Files: per-case validation and test predictions for all 235 models (score, probability, label), per-model predictions on the 6,163 LUNA25 nodules for two external analyses (pre-specified 48 mm field of view and the declared 28 mm deviation), the frozen design, all three addendum versions and the deviation record with their SHA-256 hashes, the selection record, hyperparameter search records, result tables, preparation reports, logs, the software environment and all code. A README explains every folder and how to recompute each result. LUNA25 images, identifiers and labels are not redistributed, and predictions are linked to the public LUNA25 annotation file by row number. Model weights are available from the creator on reasonable request. Hardware: one NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. Software: PyTorch 2.14.1, timm 1.0.30, Optuna 5.0.0, medmnist 3.0.2.

title: Deterministic but Wrong: Why Behavior-Based Tests Miss Structural Errors in Keccak-f Implementations
abstract: This technical note reports three implementation defects present simultaneously in our own LookingGlass v2.4.0 Keccak-f[1600] code: a reduced round count (12 instead of 24), a single-bit error in the round constant RC[22] (bit 31 miswritten as bit 15), and a transposed pi index mapping. Thirty-five internal consistency tests passed while every NIST SHA-3 Known Answer Test (KAT) vector failed. The note contributes: (i) a structure-blindness argument explaining why input-space search, metamorphic testing and statistical batteries cannot detect input-independent defects; (ii) a measured behavioral battery in which all three defects pass determinism, sensitivity, avalanche, bit-balance and collision checks; and (iii) a self-contained Python reproduction with exact digests for all three mutants. This work makes no claim about Keccak-f[1600] or SHA-3 itself; the defects are ours. It is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed. The affected library is linked under Related identifiers at a fixed commit.

title: Explainable AI for Intelligent and Sustainable Decision-Making
abstract: Organizations increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve strategic planning, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, conventional machine learning models often lack transparency, limiting managerial trust, accountability, and the practical adoption of AI-driven decisions. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates predictive analytics, interpretable machine learning, and sustainability indicators to support transparent, reliable, and evidence-based decision-making across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Evaluation uses a benchmark dataset containing operational performance, resource consumption, organizational efficiency, and environmental indicators. Comparative experiments assess predictive accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), explanation consistency, decision latency, computational cost, and sustainability performance. Baseline models include Logistic Regression, conventional Random Forest, and XGBoost without explanation mechanisms. Ablation studies examine the individual contributions of interpretability and sustainability-aware optimization. The experimental evaluation is designed to determine whether the proposed framework improves predictive reliability, explanation quality, and sustainability-aware decisions compared with conventional approaches. Quantitative reporting will include percentage improvements in predictive performance, reductions in decision latency and resource consumption, and explanation stability across repeated experiments. Qualitative analysis will assess managerial understandability, perceived trustworthiness, fairness, and practical implementation challenges. Numerical outcomes will be reported only after experiments are completed, avoiding unsupported performance claims. The proposed framework establishes a comparative approach for integrating explainability, predictive intelligence, and sustainability into organizational decision-making. By connecting model predictions with transparent explanations and measurable sustainability indicators, the framework aims to strengthen accountability, operational effectiveness, and responsible technology adoption. Future validation across multiple industries will establish its generalizability and practical value. Keywords: Predictive Analytics; Explainable Artificial Intelligence; Sustainable Decision-Making; Interpretable Machine Learning; Organizational Intelligence.

title: EL-RAKHAWI VERIFIED ASTRO-QUANTUM PROCESSING FRAMEWORK (VAQPF) A Unified Architecture for Sovereign, Mathematically Guaranteed, and Energy-Efficient Processing of Exascale Astronomical Data
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Verified Astro-Quantum Processing Framework (VAQPF) revolutionizes exascale astronomical data processing through four integrated pillars: (1) Neuro-Symbolic Astro-Filter with Bounded Formal Verification, mathematically guaranteeing signal validity within instrument noise uncertainty ($P_{valid} = P_{neural}(S|D) \times V_{bounded}(S, \Phi_{astro}, \Sigma_{noise})$), reducing false positives to <0.1% while preserving >95% of novel discoveries; (2) Topological Quantum Graph Mapper achieving polynomial-time complexity $O(poly(N) \cdot \log(1/\epsilon))$ specifically for bounded-degree structured astronomical datasets (cosmic web, N-body simulations), bypassing classical NP-hard bottlenecks; (3) Sovereign Federated Astro-Data Nodes utilizing Post-Quantum Cryptography and Incremental Verifiable Computation (IVC) with recursive zk-SNARKs, maintaining $O(\log(N_{data}))$ verification while managing prover complexity at $O(N_{batch} \cdot \log(N_{batch}))$ to prevent exascale bottlenecks; (4) Cryogenic Photonic Data Ingestion handling Terahertz bandwidths with minimal thermal dissipation. Field projections demonstrate 48-hour classical processing reduced to 15 minutes for cosmic graph mapping (10^6 nodes), 90% false positive reduction versus deep learning, and bandwidth costs slashed from $2M/month to <$50K/month through federated architecture. Protected by 6 comprehensive PCT claims covering bounded verification, structured dataset quantum mapping, incremental zk-SNARK sovereign nodes, and photonic hardware, VAQPF transforms astroinformatics from probabilistic guesswork to mathematically guaranteed, sovereign, energy-efficient cosmic discovery, ensuring humanity's exploration of the universe is built on unassailable truth within measurable bounds.

title: Argumento da Exponencialidade Lógica Axiomatica
abstract: RESUMO Apresenta-se o Argumento da Exponencialidade Lógica Axiomática [A.E.L.A.] como princípio regulador kantiano de necessidade condicional: uma ocorrência verificada sob protocolo sensível ao domínio revela viabilidade estrutural e reprodutibilidade enquanto as condições se mantiverem. O framework é definido como auto-verificável por contradição performativa de segunda ordem, com regra de demarcação explícita contra prova gödeliana e o teorema de Löb. Propõem-se critério operacional de projetibilidade para o paradoxo de Goodman, ancorado em invariância sob troca de operador, local e aparelho; distinção temporal migratória entre duas matemáticas, Produto versus Sincrônica; critério objeto versus ferramenta para verificação direta e indireta; reformulação do Cogito como Cogito Verificável de tipo por intersecção triangular; e explicitação do mecanismo do algoritmo gerativo fixo. O texto reconhece seu próprio status como Produto que descreve o Lógico. A fundação ontológica do framework integra a tradição heraclitiana do Panta Rhei, onde o Logos permanece fixo enquanto a água do rio flui, análoga à distinção entre o algoritmo gerativo invariante do Espaço Lógico e o fluxo histórico de seus ocupantes verificáveis. Essa estrutura fornece complemento ontológico à moldura regulativa kantiana: o Logos que torna possível tratar o verificável como condição de possibilidade da ciência. A trava linguística wittgensteiniana contra linguagem privada, baseada nas Investigações §§199, 202 e 243, fundamenta o Protocolo 1.1 ao exigir que seguir regra seja prática pública e não crença privada, sem critério de 2 correção. Token privado não constitui critério de passagem para Sincrônico; a forma de vida comum e a triangulação são requisitos obrigatórios para migração, pois não há mapa privado, apenas mapa bom triangulado. Hegel é incorporado como teste anti-idealismo dialético, reconhecendo que a Fenomenologia descreve corretamente o movimento dos Produtos mas confunde troca de descrição com troca de Logos. Kuhn é incorporado como teste anti-relativismo paradigmático, aceitando incomensurabilidade sociológica corrigida, isto é, tradução difícil entre paradigmas, mas rejeitando incomensurabilidade lógica total que violaria a trava wittgensteiniana. Sobre essa base, o framework organiza-se em Trilho Duplo Metodológico, com o Trilho B reformulado como conjunto de restrições sobre os procedimentos admissíveis do Trilho A, e não como camada decorativa. Institui-se o Comitê de Carimbo, com graus quantificados e independência graduada em quatro eixos, substituindo a tese segundo a qual o carimbo não é julgamento pela tese da auditabilidade do julgamento, e distinguindo explicitamente garantia epistêmica de verdade. O critério operacional de projetividade é posicionado face ao entrincheiramento goodmaniano e à invariância de Woodward. Estabelece-se tipologia das mesmas condições por unidade de previsão, com cláusula de classe de referência, análise de sensibilidade e pré-registro obrigatório, o que reclassifica a inflação cósmica como caso Tipo-2 e reformula o critério de refutação número quatro. A validação retrospectiva é reconstruída com controle de taxa-base, acurácia balanceada, área sob a curva ROC, concordância interavaliadores e janelas de consolidação calibradas por domínio. Acrescenta-se a distinção entre forma e conteúdo do protocolo como resposta ao relativismo histórico dos protocolos; a reformulação do critério de ausência de contradição em termos de resistência da evidência em vez de autoridade institucional; o caso fronteiriço da matéria escura e regras explícitas para o tratamento de dissensos científicos persistentes; o diálogo com o falsificacionismo popperiano como complementaridade hierárquica, com Popper na função de porteiro e o A.E.L.A. na função de arquiteto; e o reconhecimento explícito de questões em aberto, em substituição ao encerramento meramente triunfal. 3 Palavras-chave: Indução. Espaço Lógico. Verificação. Realismo Estrutural. Goodman. Woodward. Heráclito. Wittgenstein. Hegel. Kuhn. Popper.

title: ZEPHIRUM (ZYQL) Software Record: Trivalent Quantum Machine-Learning Language
abstract: Doctoral-scale thesis draft and the guarded software record of ZYQL, a necessity-first trivalent exact-decision language (1 / 0 / REFUSED) for computational quantum chemistry, with the Hybrid Boundary Pattern (exact offline decision; QPU as witness; ML-DSA-44 sealed receipts) validated on three real superconducting QPUs (backend and job identifiers are sealed inside the ML-DSA-44 receipts). Includes signed experiment records: H2 exact ground state certified at -1.1456 Ha; Bell positive/separable negative hardware controls; GHZ ladder to 20 qubits (sparse); CHSH S=1.2822 certified refusal. Software carries the ZYGUARD guardian: refusal-before-compute for seven prohibited purpose classes, structural purity (no execution primitives), post-quantum traceable receipts. License note: code is MIT; the thesis text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (dual licensing declared; the record-level license field reflects the dominant artifact, the software). 2026-10-24 metadata revision. The ecosystem has since evolved into ZEPHIRUM (ZYQL) v2.1.0 — a trivalent quantum machine-learning language with sealed receipts (SHA3-256, ML-DSA-44 / ML-KEM-768), REFUSED as a first-class verdict, MPS tensor-network backends and native ZNE. Test suite 66/66; worldwide launch announcement: discussions/38. Repository: SerenaSolutions/zephirum-lang · Project site: serenasolutions.github.io

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environment for Beyond-Visual-Range Air Combat
abstract: An open simulation environment is presented for training multiple reinforcement-learning agents in beyond-visual-range air combat while balancing physical fidelity against rollout speed. The objective is to provide a reproducible testbed that retains the sensing, tracking, weapon, and cooperative-information effects governing long-range engagements without the computational cost of a full mission simulator. Aircraft and missiles use geodetic four-degree-of-freedom kinematics and energy-based aerodynamics; probabilistic radar detections, electronic-warfare effects, shared-track fusion, seeker-constrained missile guidance, and distance-dependent terminal lethality are represented explicitly. Fixed-shape observations and safety-gated actions support parallel self-play. End-to-end experiments with a memoryless policy learned boundary compliance, survival, and progressively more effective weapon employment, while subsystem profiling measured approximately ten seconds of wall-clock time for a 300-step two-versus-two episode on the reported hardware. These results establish internal training readiness and reproducible computational scaling and form a platform for reproducible research on learned tactics and fair benchmarking in this domain.

End-to-end experiments with a memoryless policy learned boundary compliance, survival, and progressively more effective weapon employment, while subsystem profiling measured approximately ten seconds of wall-clock time for a 300-step two-versus-two episode on the reported hardware. These results establish internal training readiness and reproducible computational scaling and form a platform for reproducible research on learned tactics and fair benchmarking in this domain.

title: EchoAlign: bridging generative and discriminative learning under noisy labels
abstract: Noisy labels significantly hinder the accuracy and generalization of machine learning models, particularly due to ambiguous instance features. Traditional techniques that attempt to correct noisy labels directly, such as those using transition matrices, often fail to address the inherent complexities of the problem sufficiently. In this paper, we introduce EchoAlign, a transformative paradigm shift in learning from noisy labels. Instead of focusing on label correction, EchoAlign treats noisy labels (Y) as accurate and modifies corresponding instance features (X) to achieve better alignment with Y. EchoAlign's core components are (1) EchoMod: Employing controllable generative models, EchoMod precisely modifies instances while maintaining their intrinsic characteristics and ensuring alignment with the noisy labels. (2) EchoSelect: Instance modification inevitably introduces distribution shifts between training and test sets. EchoSelect maintains a significant portion of clean original instances to mitigate these shifts. It leverages the distinct feature similarity distributions between original and modified instances as a robust tool for accurate sample selection. This integrated approach yields remarkable results. In environments with 30% instance-dependent noise, even at 99% selection accuracy, EchoSelect retains nearly twice the number of samples compared to the previous best method. Notably, on three datasets, EchoAlign surpasses previous state-of-the-art techniques with a substantial improvement.

title: Photonic Neuromorphic Processing With Coupled Spiking Silicon Microrings
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the physical computing mechanisms of individual network nodes is essential for scaling neuromorphic photonic architectures. This work proposes a compact passive nonlinear photonic core based on a side‐coupled integrated spaced sequence of resonators (SCISSOR) comprising three nominally equal microrings and investigate its computing capabilities. Its nonlinearities and internal feedback enable analogue, spiking, and bistable responses that are accessed by tuning the injection power and wavelength. Implemented as a single nonlinear node in a time‐multiplexed reservoir computing, the SCISSOR achieves error‐free classification on the Iris dataset and accuracies above 97 on the Sonar task, using both analogue and digital reservoir representations with 150 virtual nodes. In the digital scheme, spiking dynamics naturally generate sparse reservoir states, enabling efficient classification even with a single spike. Intriguingly, operating points at the boundaries where sharp transitions in dynamical complexity and/or output power occur support high task‐performance, opening novel strategies for future on‐chip training. Spiking and thermal bistabilities also participate to enhance the computational performance. These results suggest that coupled optical microrings can serve as compact, physically interpretable nonlinear building blocks for future neuromorphic photonic processors, particularly in optical‐domain preprocessing and sensing scenarios where kHz‐to‐MHz signal bandwidths are relevant.

title: What WER Hides: A Closer Look at Algerian Code-Switched ASR
abstract: Automatic speech recognition for Algerian social-media speech is hard because of dialectal variation, Arabic-French code-switching, and non-standard orthography, yet these difficulties are usually summarised by a single word error rate that hides where recognition fails and whether gains reach information-bearing content. We evaluate seven systems on roughly 30 minutes of Algerian political social-media speech, annotated by language variety as Algerian dialect, Modern Standard Arabic, codeswitched, or French: a Whisper-large-v3 baseline, five Whisper variants fine-tuned on different combinations of broadcast, dialectal, and code-switched speech, and the prompted Qwen3-Omni model. The best system reduces overall WER from 60.1% to 31.3%, but still reaches 44.0% on code-switched speech, and named entities remain harder than ordinary tokens, with fewer than half preserved. These results show that ASR difficulty on Algerian social-media speech cannot be read from overall WER alone; it must be measured separately by language variety and by whether named entities survive.

title: Anomaly Detection using Source-Reversed Flow Matching
abstract: Anomaly detection in textual data remains an underexplored problem, hindered by fragmented benchmarks, scarce labeled data, and methods that fail to model the distribution of normal text in a continuous and generative manner. We propose FLOCAT 1 , an unsupervised approach that reformulates this task through a source-reversed flow matching paradigm: rather than learning to generate, we learn a flow from inlier text embeddings toward a lowvariance isotropic Gaussian target, whose radius is explicitly constrained to ensure that the distance to the centroid serves as a geometrically consistent anomaly score. Built on a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone, FLO-CAT operates at both token and sentence level through a level-agnostic interpolation mechanism, enabling fine-grained signal interpretability. We evaluate on 10 datasets spanning text classification, spam detection, sentiment analysis, human-vs. machine-generated text and depression screening, consistently achieving state-of-the-art AUC-ROC across all benchmarks and text representations.

title: Enhancing Fraud Detection in Banking: A Hybrid Approach Combining Graph Algorithms and Machine Learning
abstract: Financial institutions face significant losses from increasingly sophisticated fraud attacks that evade traditional detection methods. This study proposes a hybrid approach combining machine learning (ML) (XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, k-NN) with graph algorithms (PageRank, Community Detection, Degree Centrality) to enhance fraud detection accuracy in banking transactions. Using the BankSim dataset containing 587,443 legitimate and 7,200 fraudulent transactions we first address class imbalance through under sampling, then integrate graph-based features extracted via Neo4j to capture complex transactional relationships. Our methodology demonstrates that combining graph analytics with machine learning yields superior performance compared to standalone models, achieving precision scores up to 0.93 (k-NN) and recall rates of 0.87 (XGBoost). The hybrid approach also reduces training and prediction times by 2.9% and 6.8%, respectively, validated through 5-fold cross-validation. Key findings highlight that graph-augmented features improve F1-scores by 4–7% over conventional methods, with Random Forest and k-NN showing the most significant gains. This work contributes a practical framework for financial institutions to leverage interconnected transaction data, balancing detection accuracy (minimizing false negatives) and operational efficiency (reducing false positives). Future directions include testing this approach on real-time transaction streams and expanding to multi-modal fraud detection.

title: Are Benchmarks a source of bias in LLMs? MMLU, CommonSenseQA and MGSM under the Microscope
abstract: Evaluation is an essential process in the development and use of NLP systems. Benchmarks are widely used to calibrate systems, determine the efficiency of techniques, but also to advertise recently launched language models. Not only do benchmarks allow for evaluation and system comparisons, but they are also commonly utilized as training and validation corpora. In this paper, we aim at characterizing the "world knowledge" that is put forth by benchmarks by closely inspecting their content. Through qualitative manual annotations (+15k instances) as well as quantitative automatic analyses, we uncover the presence of both explicit and implicit biases in MMLU, Common-SenseQA and MGSM, ranging from representational imbalance to bluntly sexist and racist instances. Our findings demonstrate that current NLP evaluation practices pose numerous quality issues, reinforce stereotypes and even contain explicitly harmful content. The current operationalization of benchmarks is questioned, and we provide recommendations and directions for further ethical evaluation.

title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) depend fundamentally on the diversity, depth, and factual rigor of their pre-training corpora. However, contemporary foundational pre-training datasets (such as The Pile, S2ORC, and Dolma) exhibit a severe structural omission: African scientific, medical, legal, and agricultural scholarship constitutes less than 0.5% of global pre-training tokens. Consequently, state-of-the-art models suffer from systematic failure modes when reasoning about tropical epidemiology, localized smallholder agro-ecologies, regional economic governance, and indigenous linguistic structures. To resolve this representation deficit and advance African intellectual sovereignty in artificial intelligence, we introduce Africa-Papers, the largest curated multi-domain Pan-African academic pre-training corpus to date. Comprising over 844,807 full-text papers spanning 10.15 billion tokens across 879 Parquet shards, Africa-Papers unifies four primary scientific streams: (1) continental peer-reviewed journals indexed in DOAJ across 31 African nations, (2) the CGIAR CGSpace agricultural repository, (3) African-authored and African-focused STEM/AI preprints on arXiv, and (4) open-access international publications by scholars affiliated with African institutions indexed via OpenAlex. The entire corpus is processed into layout-aware, clean Markdown preserving section hierarchies, mathematical equations, and tabular data, accompanied by exact BPE token counts and a standardized 8-domain taxonomy. We release Africa-Papers openly on the Hugging Face Hub under the AfriSpeech organization to accelerate continual pre-training and domain evaluation for foundation models globally.

title: Sparse-station temperature interpolation via Gaussian-process committees: an artificial intelligence evaluation of variance-inflation risk in national heat-health alert triggering
abstract: Heat-health alert systems in data-sparse national settings depend on interpolated temperature fields whose uncertainty is rarely propagated into the trigger decision. The analysis treats a committee of local Gaussian-process experts as a weighted product-of-experts and derives the committee predictive variance as a quadratic form in the per-expert variances, with an inflation factor that grows with the disagreement between expert means and shrinks with the trace of the committee weight matrix. A decision-theoretic framework is then constructed in which the alert trigger is a threshold on the posterior mean and the variance inflation enters through the probability of correct triggering. Using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Harare over 2000-2023 (312 monthly observations, mean 18.914 C, standard deviation 3.107 C, warming trend 0.2001 C per decade), the paper shows that the observed interannual variability is of the same order as the inflation the committee architecture can introduce, so that trigger reliability is sensitive to committee design rather than to the interpolation bias alone. The contribution is a formal criterion for bounding committee-induced variance inflation in sparse-station interpolation and a demonstration that alert-trigger reliability should be evaluated against the inflation bound rather than against point-estimate accuracy.

title: Differentially private federated crop-yield benchmarking across sovereign agricultural registries: a privacy-utility frontier analysis for climate analytics competition policy
abstract: Sovereign agricultural registries hold the crop-yield records that climate-analytics competition policy needs, yet the same records are personal data whose release is constrained by national privacy law. The framework combines a federated Laplace and Gaussian mechanism with a stratified yield model, and derives the sensitivity of benchmark statistics to the number of participating registries and the per-registry clipping bound. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis of NASA POWER monthly air-temperature reanalysis for Accra, Ghana (2000-2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 26.521 C, warming trend 0.1622 C per decade), which supplies the climate covariate that a yield benchmark would condition on. Competition policy for climate analytics should regulate the privacy-utility frontier directly, rather than mandating either data sharing or data localisation.

title: Knowledge-distilled decentralized federated learning for privacy-preserving medical image analysis
abstract: Federated learning (FL) has proved to be a potential way for decentralized medical institutions to collaborate on model training while preserving data privacy. However, traditional FL approaches rely on centralized aggregation and frequent weight sharing, which pose scalability, robustness, and privacy challenges particularly in medical imaging tasks involving classification and segmentation under non-IID conditions. This paper presents. Our method works without a central server, transmits only temperature-scaled soft predictions computed on a shared public reference set rather than raw weights or gradients. KD-DFL eliminates the central aggregator while matching server-based FedAvg under IID data (0.90 accuracy/0.83 Dice, within 0.002). Under non-IID partitioning, it recovers 55 to 67% of the gap between isolated training and FedAvg. Communication shrinks by 7 times compared to model transmission, and membership-inference accuracy falls to near-random levels (54.2% vs. 74.6% centralized. These results indicate that consensus in prediction space is a practical substitute for parameter aggregation in decentralized, privacy-preserving, multi-task federated learning for real-world medical AI systems.

title: A Multimetric Evaluation of Ensemble and Neural Models for Imbalanced Credit Scoring on the German Credit Dataset
abstract: Credit scoring models must balance global discrimination, minority-class detection, probability quality, and computational efficiency, particularly when default cases are less frequent than non-default cases. This study benchmarks Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Multilayer Perceptron using the German Credit Dataset, which contains 1,000 borrower records. All models were evaluated using a consistent preprocessing, partitioning, and imbalance-aware training protocol. Performance was assessed through ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Balanced Accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Brier Score, and computational time. The results indicate moderate predictive performance across the evaluated models. XGBoost achieved the highest global discrimination with a ROC-AUC of 0.764, whereas the MLP obtained the highest PR-AUC of 0.378 and the lowest Brier Score of 0.123, indicating the best native probability quality among the evaluated models. No post-hoc probability calibration was applied. However, the MLP produced lower recall at the selected classification threshold. Logistic Regression required the least computation but recorded the lowest ROC-AUC and PR-AUC. Exploratory SHAP analysis was used to identify influential borrower attributes. These benchmark-specific findings demonstrate that model selection depends on the intended decision objective rather than architectural complexity alone.

evidence.title: A Multimetric Evaluation of Ensemble and Neural Models for Imbalanced Credit Scoring on the German Credit Dataset
evidence.abstract: Credit scoring models must balance global discrimination, minority-class detection, probability quality, and computational efficiency, particularly when default cases are less frequent than non-default cases. This study benchmarks Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Multilayer Perceptron using the German Credit Dataset, which contains 1,000 borrower records. All models were evaluated using a consistent preprocessing, partitioning, and imbalance-aware training protocol. Performance was assessed through ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Balanced Accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Brier Score, and computational time. The results indicate moderate predictive performance across the evaluated models. XGBoost achieved the highest global discrimination with a ROC-AUC of 0.764, whereas the MLP obtained the highest PR-AUC of 0.378 and the lowest Brier Score of 0.123, indicating the best native probability quality among the evaluated models. No post-hoc probability calibration was applied. However, the MLP produced lower recall at the selected classification threshold. Logistic Regression required the least computation but recorded the lowest ROC-AUC and PR-AUC. Exploratory SHAP analysis was used to identify influential borrower attributes. These benchmark-specific findings demonstrate that model selection depends on the intended decision objective rather than architectural complexity alone.

title: An Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Symbolic-Lexicon Framework for Multi-Domain Sentiment Classification
abstract: Multi-domain sentiment classifiers may return a polarity label even when the evidence behind that decision becomes fragile under domain shift. This study evaluates an uncertainty-aware hybrid symbolic-lexicon framework designed to pair each polarity prediction with a traceable accept-or-defer status. The framework combines a lexical branch adapted only on training data with training-only fitted symbolic feature states, variable-precision rough evidence, and nested score fusion. Evaluation uses the UCI Sentiment Labelled Sentences dataset, comprising 3,000 balanced English sentences from Amazon Cells, IMDb, and Yelp, under repeated within-source, pooled multi-domain, and leave-one-source-out protocols. In pooled evaluation, the framework achieved 83.73% accuracy and 83.76% F1-score, improving F1 by 0.50 points over the adaptive lexical branch. The boundary mechanism deferred 53.55% of cases and retained 92.54% accuracy among accepted predictions; however, matched-coverage logistic regression and SVM confidence rankings produced lower selective risk. The contribution is therefore a reproducible, algorithmically traceable polarity-and-deferment mechanism rather than a claim of universal predictive or uncertainty-ranking superiority.

title: Calibrated Is Not Informative: What a Fall in Expected Calibration Error Shows About LLM Confidence, Why Verbalised Scores Fail on Resolution as Well as Level, and the Recalibration Baseline the Ensembling Results Omit
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research A common finding in work on language-model confidence is that a model asked to state its own confidence in one pass is badly overconfident, and that some added procedure - sampling several answers, a separate critique pass, a longer chain of thought - repairs it. The repair is usually scored by expected calibration error (ECE). A 2026 telecommunications study is a clear recent case: it reports that averaging several blind self-evaluations of a reasoning chain cuts ECE by up to 88 percent on three telecom benchmarks, and it reports no discrimination metric. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that such claims mix two failures that need different fixes. One is level: the scores sit too high on average. The other is resolution: the scores barely separate right answers from wrong ones. ECE mostly measures level. It can reach zero for a constant score that separates nothing, and a monotone map fitted on held-out labels can remove most level error without changing the ranking at all. In the published studies that report both ECE and a ranking metric, the two move independently. Better prompts cut ECE while, in the authors' summary, AUROC stayed close to chance. Verbalised scores cut ECE on one benchmark by three quarters while the area under the selective accuracy curve rose by about one point. Sampling several answers raised AUROC from 54.8 to 92.7 on arithmetic but by one point on a yes-no reasoning set, and a separate self-evaluation pass, the mechanism the telecom method repeats, was at chance on the one multiple-choice set where it was measured alone. Re-reading the telecom study's own tables, the author finds that its top confidence tier was about three points more accurate than the pooled base rate, and that its largest ECE reduction comes from a 150-item subset, where binning noise alone is close to the reported post-method value. The paper gives a decision procedure and five tests that would separate what added inference passes buy from what a cheap recalibration already buys.

title: Comparative Machine Learning Bias Correction of Satellite-Derived Solar Irradiance at Tropical Stations in Central Java, Indonesia
abstract: Satellite-derived Global Horizontal Irradiance products carry systematic bias in tropical regions, so site-level correction is a prerequisite for their use where ground networks are sparse. This study compares bias-correction methods for NASA POWER daily irradiance in Central Java, Indonesia, and asks how much reported accuracy reflects algebraic dependence between predictors and the ground reference. Ten PUSDATARU stations were analysed over 2020–2024 (17,072 station-days; 8,459 from five exactly co-located stations). Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Elastic Net, and Quantile Mapping were trained chronologically (2020–2022/2023/2024) against persistence and climatology baselines, with preprocessing fitted on training data only, paired significance tests, leave-one-station-out validation, and SHAP attribution. Random Forest reduced RMSE from 3.398 to 2.674 MJ m⁻² day⁻¹ (21.3%), lowered mean bias from 0.988 to 0.221, and raised R² from 0.266 to 0.546; across ten stations XGBoost reduced error from 5.921 to 2.831. Differences among tree ensembles were not statistically robust, and the weighted ensemble gave no gain at the highest inference cost. Adding ground-observed sunshine as a predictor raised the coefficient of determination to 0.9994, identified as recovery of the Ångström–Prescott expression defining the reference (70.9% attribution). Near-perfect accuracies against sunshine-derived references therefore measure leakage, not skill; correction also failed to transfer spatially, motivating sub-degree geostationary products as the next step.

title: Comparative Classification of DNS-over-HTTPS Traffic on the CIRACIC-DoHBrw-2020 Dataset Using Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost
abstract: DNS over HTTPS (DoH) improves the confidentiality of domain-name resolution but reduces the visibility available to enterprise monitoring and security systems because DNS is carried within encrypted HTTPS traffic. This study compares Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost for distinguishing DoH from non-DoH HTTPS traffic while examining predictive performance, computational cost, and model interpretability. The models were evaluated using the cleaned Layer 1 representation of the CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 dataset, which contains 1,019,117 flow records and 29 statistical predictors. The controlled protocol used three repeated 80:20 stratified development-test splits (seeds 42, 52, and 62), three-fold cross-validation, class-imbalance treatment, held-out testing, execution-time measurement, and permutation importance. Random Forest produced the strongest threshold-dependent results, achieving a macro F1 of 0.9965, MCC of 0.9930, and false-positive rate of 0.0011. XGBoost obtained the highest Average Precision (0.9994) and required a mean training time of 31.40 seconds, approximately 95.8% lower than Random Forest (743.42 seconds). Logistic Regression was computationally efficient but yielded lower DoH precision and a false-positive rate of 0.1197. PacketLengthMode was the most influential feature for both tree-based models. The results demonstrate strong within-benchmark separation, but they do not establish cross-network or operational generalisation.

title: Sparse Gaussian-process emulation of regional climate projections with active budget allocation: a computer-science evaluation of tail-quantile fidelity in adaptation screening
abstract: Sparse Gaussian-process emulators are increasingly proposed as surrogates for expensive regional climate model ensembles, but their fidelity in the distributional tails—where adaptation decisions are actually made—remains poorly characterised. The framework is evaluated on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023, 312 observations), where the mean temperature was 26.414 °C and the warming trend was 0.1553 °C per decade. The analysis formalises tail-quantile risk as a weighted integrated quantile discrepancy, derives a variational lower bound that decomposes into a global fit term and a tail-sensitive term, and shows that uniform budget allocation is provably suboptimal under mild conditions on the tail weight. A greedy active-allocation algorithm is proposed and its submodularity established, yielding a (1−1/e) approximation guarantee. Tail-quantile fidelity should be treated as a first-class design objective in climate-emulator construction, and that active budget allocation offers a principled route to improving tail performance without increasing simulator cost. The contribution is a computer-science evaluation framework, not an empirical validation of any deployed emulator.

title: Adversarial-robustness certification of flood-susceptibility classifiers under projected land-cover regime shift: a computer-science evaluation of false-negative exposure in municipal zoning analytics
abstract: Flood-susceptibility classifiers used in municipal zoning are typically validated on historical land-cover distributions, yet zoning decisions bind future development under land-cover regimes that differ from those on which the classifiers were trained. the present analysis formalises the resulting certification problem as one of bounding the false-negative rate of a learned classifier under a projected covariate shift induced by land-cover regime change. A distributionally robust certification framework is developed in which the shift is represented by a Wasserstein ball around the empirical feature distribution, and a tractable upper bound on the false-negative rate is derived via a Lipschitz-continuous surrogate of the classifier's decision boundary. The bound is shown to be tight under a margin condition and to degrade gracefully as the radius of the shift ball grows. A case study using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature for Harare, Zimbabwe (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 18.914 °C, warming trend 0.2001 °C per decade) illustrates how a slow climatic drift can be encoded as a sequence of shift radii and how the certified false-negative bound responds. The analysis indicates that classifiers with high nominal accuracy can nonetheless carry substantial certified false-negative exposure under plausible land-cover projections, and that the exposure is concentrated in the decision-boundary region where zoning stakes are highest. The contribution is a certification procedure that municipal analytics teams can apply before deploying a susceptibility classifier under a projected regime shift, together with a formal characterisation of when such certification is informative and when it is vacuous.

title: Anexo - Python: Parte 3
abstract: Este capítulo serve como uma etapa preparatória para o estudo de estruturas bidimensionais e matrizes, focando na consolidação teórica e prática sobre listas unidimensionais (vetores) em Python. O texto destaca as características dinâmicas, ordenadas e mutáveis das listas, apresentando operações fundamentais como alocação por índices inteiros, adição de elementos com o método append, iteração de laços e medição do tamanho com a função len. Além disso, revisa conceitos como o uso de acumuladores para cálculo de soma e média, o produto escalar na álgebra linear computacional e propõe um conjunto de exercícios práticos que englobam leitura de dados, inversão de listas, busca de maior e menor valor com seus respectivos índices, separação de pares/ímpares e geração de vetores nulos para inicialização de linhas.

title: Explainable hybrid ensemble framework for lung cancer classification using deep CNNs and random forest
abstract: Lung cancer is still a significant cause of cancer death in the world. Thoracic computed tomography (CT) classification can be helpful in earlier diagnosis and better patient management. However, many deep-learning techniques require large annotated datasets, large amounts of computational resources and the techniques are not easily interpretable. This manuscript introduces a comprehensible hybrid approach to multiclass lung cancer classification based on two different transfer-learning backbones, DenseNet169 and MobileNetV2. They used several ensemble techniques to combine their class-probability outputs. For qualitative visual explanations of the image regions contributing to each prediction, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to the image after inference. The framework was evaluated with two publicly available thoracic CT datasets that include both benign and malignant, normal and non-small-cell lung cancer categories. The accuracy of the Random Forest stacker for the Chest CT dataset was 99.50% and 99.54% for the IQ-OTH/NCCD dataset. The results show that DenseNet169 and MobileNetV2 complementary probability outputs could be used as an effective decision-fusion method in lung cancer classification from different datasets with different class structures and diagnostic categories. The Grad-CAM technique also made the model predictions more transparent by identifying image areas that influenced the prediction. In general, the proposed framework presents a practical and comprehensible method for automated lung cancer classification, and serves as a valuable guideline in future studies regarding the development of robust, explainable, and clinically relevant computer-aided diagnosis in medical imaging.

title: Graph-Enhanced Knowledge Tracing for Explainable Learner Modeling: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) has become a central approach for modeling students' evolving knowledge states, but conventional sequence-based KT models offer limited representation of relationships among skills, concepts, and assessment indicators, reducing their interpretability for monitoring mastery and learning progression. This study systematically reviews how graph-based and knowledge graph-enhanced KT models have been developed, integrated, and evaluated to support skill mastery, learning outcome monitoring, and assessment-related interpretation. A PRISMA-based Systematic Literature Review was conducted using Scopus and IEEE Xplore, covering publications indexed from 2015 to 2025. From 116 initial records, 20 studies satisfied the eligibility criteria for active graph-enhanced KT and were included in the synthesis corpus, comprising 8 core (40.0%) and 12 supporting (60.0%) studies. Six major integration families were identified, including GCN/GNN-based, Knowledge Graph/ontology-enhanced, heterogeneous or multiplex graph, attention-over-graph, Q-matrix/concept map-based KT, and graph-supported recommendation. Graph-enhanced KT can enrich learner-state representation, support skill and mastery interpretation, and strengthen explainable learner modeling, particularly among core studies. However, active graph-KT integration remains limited, and issues of construct validity, cross-domain generalization, fairness, and deployment-oriented evaluation remain underexplored.

title: Federated learning for climate-model downscaling across data-scarce national meteorological services: a differential-privacy evaluation of forecast skill and sovereign data leakage
abstract: National meteorological services in data-scarce regions face a structural tension: statistical downscaling of coarse climate-model output requires large, pooled training corpora, yet the station records that would supply such corpora are sovereign assets whose transfer across borders is legally and politically constrained. Federated learning has been proposed as a resolution, but its privacy guarantees are usually asserted rather than quantified, and the trade-off between forecast skill and sovereign data leakage has not been formalised. The framework couples a formal leakage bound under (ε, δ)-differential privacy to a skill-degradation model for the downscaling task, and derives the conditions under which a federated, noise-perturbed ensemble retains useful forecast skill while bounding sovereign exposure. The privacy budget, not the federation topology, is the binding constraint on skill, and that the leakage bound is governed by the composition of local updates rather than by the number of participating services. The contribution is a formal, testable account of the skill–sovereignty frontier that national meteorological services can use to set privacy budgets before committing to federated infrastructure.

title: Differentially private computed generation of household energy-consumption microdata for urban heat-vulnerability mapping: a computer-science evaluation of equity-audit distortion under DP budgets
abstract: Differential privacy (DP) is increasingly proposed as the mechanism by which household energy microdata can be released for climate-analytics applications such as urban heat-vulnerability mapping, yet the distortion that DP noise introduces into equity audits of those data has not been characterised formally. It formalises the equity-audit statistic as a weighted function of household-level energy indicators and derives an upper bound on the sensitivity of that statistic to the replacement of a single household record, showing that the bound scales with the maximum household weight and with the range of the energy indicator. The bound is then propagated through the Gaussian and Laplace mechanisms to obtain closed-form expressions for the noise scale required to achieve a target (ε, δ)-guarantee, and the resulting mean-squared distortion of the audit statistic is expressed as a function of ε, the number of households, and the weight concentration. The analysis is anchored in the real DHS Program indicator 'Households possessing a computer' (HC_HEFF_H_CMP), which is used to characterise the empirical distribution of a household-level digital-access covariate across 27 African countries and 56 country-survey observations between 2015 and 2025 (mean 7.893, standard deviation 5.144, minimum Guinea 1.50, maximum South Africa 22.00).

The analysis is anchored in the real DHS Program indicator 'Households possessing a computer' (HC_HEFF_H_CMP), which is used to characterise the empirical distribution of a household-level digital-access covariate across 27 African countries and 56 country-survey observations between 2015 and 2025 (mean 7.893, standard deviation 5.144, minimum Guinea 1.50, maximum South Africa 22.00).

title: Graph-matching domain adaptation for cross-border cropland masks: an artificial intelligence evaluation of label-scarcity transfer failure in national agricultural statistics
abstract: Cross-border transfer of cropland masks is routinely proposed as a remedy for label scarcity in national agricultural statistics, yet the conditions under which graph-matching domain adaptation fails have not been formalised. The analysis treats label scarcity as a structural property of the target domain rather than a sampling deficiency, and derives a bound on target risk that separates three additive components: graph-matching distortion, label-scarcity variance, and the divergence between source and target cropland definitions. The bound is used to identify a transfer-failure threshold below which adaptation is dominated by the unadapted source classifier. A formal proposition establishes that graph-matching distortion grows with the spectral gap between source and target adjacency structures, and a corollary shows that this distortion is not reduced by increasing the number of unlabelled target samples. The paper does not report empirical estimates; it provides the formal apparatus, the failure criterion, and the diagnostic quantities that a national statistical office would need to compute before adopting a transferred mask. The contribution is a specification of when cross-border graph-matching adaptation should be rejected, and a set of computable indicators that make that rejection auditable.

title: Multi-scale LSTM forecasting with attention-based feature fusion for anomaly detection in multivariate monitoring data
abstract: Abstract Engineering systems such as power equipment and industrial processes are monitored through multivariate time series whose anomalies appear at different temporal scales, from short fluctuations to deviations that persist over a whole operating cycle. A detector that reads a single input window has to commit to one of these scales. This paper presents MAF-LSTM, a forecasting-based anomaly detection framework in which parallel long short-term memory (LSTM) branches read input windows of different lengths, a scale-level attention module fuses their representations into a one-step-ahead forecast, and the forecasting residuals are scored with the Mahalanobis distance estimated on normal validation data. Experiments on smart meter data, two sets of high-voltage converter modulator pulses and a simulated chemical process show that MAF-LSTM achieves the highest AU-ROC and AU-PR of the five compared methods on all four datasets, exceeding the best baseline by 3.20 and 5.33 percentage points on average. An ablation study on the smart meter data quantifies the contribution of each component and shows that multi-scale modeling is most beneficial for anomalies with pronounced within-day fluctuation, where it matches or exceeds the best single-window model on each anomaly type without requiring the window length to be tuned.

title: Effects of Adversarial Training of Word Embeddings on Chinese Agricultural Pest and Disease Named Entity Recognition with BERT-CRF
abstract: Entity boundaries, confusable entity types and surface forms absent from the training data all make it harder to extract structured information from agricultural pest and disease texts. We examined whether single-step adversarial training of word embeddings with the fast gradient method (FGM) improves entity recognition when the BERT-CRF inference architecture is left unchanged. On the official 13-type AgCNER corpus, with exact matching of character span and entity type, we compared a feature-based CRF, BiLSTM-CRF, BERT-CRF and BERT-CRF+FGM, training each neural model with three fixed random seeds. BERT-CRF+FGM reached mean test precision, recall and F1 of 94.37%, 95.10% and 94.73%. Its F1 was 0.28 percentage points higher than that of the matched BERT-CRF baseline, and the paired difference was positive for every seed. F1 on unseen surface forms rose from 74.87% to 76.41%, and the overall gain remained 0.27 percentage points after test texts duplicated in other splits were removed. Mean F1 increased for 11 of the 13 types but fell for Company and Organization. FGM did not change the parameter count. The seed-42 model produced 20,670 indexed entity occurrences that can be checked against the released records and character spans. The official test set had been used in an earlier baseline study and test results informed model adoption, so these findings are exploratory; independently sourced data are needed to assess how far they generalize.

title: Federated learning of crop-disease classifiers across quarantine-silenced phytosanitary archives: a computer-science evaluation of privacy-utility trade-offs for cross-border outbreak analytics
abstract: Phytosanitary archives hold the labelled crop-disease observations that cross-border outbreak analytics require, yet quarantine regulation, commercial confidentiality and national data sovereignty keep those archives closed to centralised training. the present analysis formalises federated learning over such archives as a constrained optimisation problem in which each participating authority trains a local classifier on its own held-out data and shares only parameter updates under a differential-privacy mechanism. The framework is evaluated analytically rather than empirically: we derive a Rényi-differential-privacy accountant for the interleaved Gaussian mechanism, bound the generalisation gap of the federated averaged classifier as a function of archive heterogeneity and privacy budget, and characterise the privacy-utility frontier as a Pareto surface whose curvature is governed by the number of participating archives and the Dirichlet concentration of their label distributions. The analysis is illustrated with a reanalysis of NASA POWER MERRA-2 monthly air temperature for Kampala, Uganda (0.35° N, 32.58° E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a linear warming trend of −0.1564 °C per decade, used here only to fix the climatic covariate distribution under which the classifier operates. The contribution is a decision procedure that lets a regional plant-protection organisation choose a privacy budget, an archive-participation set and a communication round count that together meet a stated outbreak-detection utility target without centralising any raw observation.

title: Hybrid IF–GNN–IF Framework for Suspected Fraud Detection in Bank Switching Transactions
abstract: Fraud detection in financial transactions remains a major challenge in the banking industry, particularly in bank switching systems that process high transaction volumes and involve complex interactions among transaction entities. This study proposes a hybrid Isolation Forest–Graph Neural Network–Isolation Forest (IF–GNN–IF) framework to identify suspected fraudulent transactions in bank switching data. In the first stage, Isolation Forest detects potentially anomalous transactions and produces anomaly scores that are used to construct pseudo-labels. In the second stage, a Graph Neural Network learns relational patterns from a transaction graph by integrating original transaction attributes with the pseudo-labels. In the final stage, the learned graph embeddings are combined with the original transaction features and evaluated using a second Isolation Forest to generate final anomaly scores. The framework was evaluated using 71,873 bank switching transaction records and achieved an accuracy of 0.9668, precision of 0.9200, recall of 0.3681, and an F1-score of 0.5258. The high precision indicates that the framework effectively identifies suspicious transaction patterns. However, the relatively low recall suggests that some suspected fraud cases remain undetected. Therefore, further validation using confirmed fraud labels is necessary to assess the practical effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed framework in real-world banking environments.

title: Enhanced Particle Swarm Sparrow Search Optimization for Aircraft Aerodynamic Parameter Identification
abstract: Abstract Accurate aerodynamic parameter identification is fundamental to achieving high-performance model‍-based aircraft control. To address the inherent challenges in this domain, this study introduces a novel hybrid optimization algorithm, the improved chaos particle swarm sparrow search algorithm (ICPSSSA), which synergistically combines the global search capabilities of the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) with the fine-tuning efficiency of particle swarm optimization (PSO). ICPSSSA enhances the optimization performance through three key innovations: the Kent chaotic map, which increases population diversity; an adaptive dynamic search mechanism, which balances exploration and exploitation, and the Lévy flight perturbation, which expands the global search radius. These components work in concert to accelerate convergence while avoiding local optima. By framing aerodynamic parameter identification as a nonlinear optimization problem, ICPSSSA was applied to both simulation scenarios and real flight data. The comparative results demonstrate that ICPSSSA consistently achieves superior accuracy, robustness, and convergence efficiency over conventional approaches, underscoring its promise as a powerful tool for high-fidelity aircraft modeling and control.

title: Evaluation of TF-IDF and Word2Vec Representations Using Support Vector Machine for Multiclass Product Category Classification of Tokopedia Reviews
abstract: As electronic commerce continues to expand, customer reviews have become an important source for automated text classification. This research evaluates and compares TF-IDF and Word2Vec representations for multiclass product category classification with Support Vector Machine (SVM). The experiment used the Tokopedia Product Reviews 2025 dataset containing 65,543 reviews across six product categories. After text preprocessing and keyword-based text refinement, 11,239 relevant reviews were retained. The dataset was divided into 80% training sets and 20% hold-out test sets. The reviews were transformed using TF-IDF and Word2Vec, while SMOTE was applied to the training data to handle the imbalance among product categories. Classification performance was assessed through five-fold cross-validation and a hold-out test set based on accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, and macro F1-score. Five-fold cross-validation showed that TF-IDF achieved mean accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, and macro F1-score of 95.95%, 93.13%, 92.78%, and 92.93%, respectively, compared with 90.80%, 84.58%, 86.02%, and 85.19% for Word2Vec. On the hold-out test set, TF-IDF achieved 95.42% accuracy and 91.88% macro F1-score, while Word2Vec achieved 91.01% and 84.91%, respectively. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielded a p-value of 0.0625, indicating no statistically significant difference at the 5% significance level. Nevertheless, TF-IDF consistently achieved higher descriptive performance than Word2Vec.

title: Deterministic reservoir computing for subseasonal rainfall forecasting under model-structure misspecification: a computer-science evaluation of forecast-value loss in rainfed advisory services
abstract: Subseasonal rainfall forecasts underpin rainfed agricultural advisories, yet the forecast systems that reach advisory services are typically evaluated on statistical accuracy rather than on the economic value of the decisions they inform. The central problem is model-structure misspecification: when the reservoir's assumed dynamical form departs from the generating process, forecast errors are not merely larger but differently structured, and the mapping from error structure to decision loss is nonlinear. The paper formalises forecast-value loss for a threshold-triggered advisory, derives a bound relating reservoir spectral radius and readout conditioning to the divergence between forecast-error and decision-loss orderings, and shows that two reservoirs with identical mean squared error can produce materially different advisory value. A methodological protocol is proposed for evaluating deterministic reservoir forecasters against decision-relevant criteria rather than accuracy alone. The contribution is a formal and methodological reframing of reservoir-computing evaluation for climate advisory services, with implications for how forecast value is reported to agricultural extension systems.

title: Anexo - Matrizes em Python
abstract: Este capítulo aborda os conceitos matemáticos e práticos de matrizes e sua implementação em Python, cobrindo desde as definições fundamentais de tipos (como matriz quadrada, identidade e nula), operações algébricas (adição, subtração, multiplicação por escalar, produto matricial) e cálculo de determinantes (pela regra 2x2 e Regra de Sarrus), até a manipulação direta de arquivos (txt e csv) através do comando with e do módulo csv. Além disso, o texto detalha a instalação e o uso das bibliotecas NumPy e Pandas, demonstrando na prática a criação de arranjos multidimensionais, a execução de cálculo matricial e a manipulação estruturada de dados tabulares utilizando DataFrames para leitura, seleção, filtragem e exportação.

title: Provenance-audited retrieval-augmented generation for national adaptation reporting: a computer-science evaluation of citation-fabrication risk in climate analytics pipelines
abstract: National adaptation reporting under the Paris Agreement requires climate-analytics pipelines that can trace every quantitative claim to a verifiable source. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offers a way to ground narrative synthesis in a document corpus, but its citation behaviour under adversarial or sparse retrieval conditions remains uncharacterised. The framework defines a provenance graph over retrieved passages and generated claims, and introduces a fabrication-risk score that combines retrieval coverage, citation-claim entailment probability, and source-identity stability. A replication-based evaluation across 1,000 computed reporting tasks shows that fabrication risk rises sharply when retrieval coverage falls below 0.6 and when the corpus contains near-duplicate documents with conflicting metadata. The analysis identifies a coverage–fabrication trade-off that is invisible to standard RAG evaluation metrics such as answer accuracy or BLEU. The contribution is a formal, auditable risk model that national reporting teams can apply before deploying RAG in adaptation-pipeline workflows.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Mapping of Google Reviews for Digital Reputation Insights of Private Higher Education Institutions in Padang City
abstract: Online reviews provide public feedback for higher education institutions, but overall star ratings cannot explain which institutional aspects shape public perception. This study aims to provide partial and aspect-specific digital reputation insights for five private higher education institutions in Padang City through aspect-based sentiment mapping of textual Google Reviews. Using Outscraper, 1,159 Google Review records were collected. After excluding 794 star-only reviews, 365 textual reviews were retained and transformed into 484 aspect-level records across five aspects: academic and lecturers, campus facilities, administrative services, environment and location, and general/others. The dataset was highly imbalanced, with 443 positive records (91.53%), 35 negative records (7.23%), and 6 neutral records (1.24%). Sentiment classification was evaluated using TF-IDF with Logistic Regression, TF-IDF with SVM, and IndoBERT through 5-fold stratified cross-validation. IndoBERT achieved the strongest performance, with an accuracy of 0.973, balanced accuracy of 0.710, macro F1-score of 0.760, and weighted F1-score of 0.971. The findings show that aspect-based sentiment mapping can support Google Review-based public perception monitoring by producing a university–aspect–sentiment map for the selected institutions. These findings are limited to textual Google Reviews from five selected institutions and should be validated using larger and more balanced datasets.
